answer: Capacity-decay registration curve. Each new identity at an address must hold a basalt-weighted storage slot whose required size grows with the count already registered there; slot demand resets only on real transfer. A violet marker tags each slot to its address, so cloning forces the attacker to buy progressively larger storage at rising spot prices. Harbor reserve caps let honest agents front-load cheaply. Marginal cost per sybil rises sharply, making N fakes cost superlinearly more than N honest registrations.
